Previously, a subtotal equal to minimum_cents would qualify for the coupon (subtotal < minimum_cents evaluates to False); now it raises ValueError because subtotal <= minimum_cents evaluates to True. This breaks expected business logic where meeting the minimum threshold should qualify for the discount.
trigger_condition: When cart subtotal equals exactly coupon.minimum_cents

title: Cart.add replaces quantity instead of accumulating
explanation: The add method now overwrites the existing quantity rather than adding to it. Previously used `self._quantities.get(sku, 0) + quantity` which accumulated quantities for repeated additions of the same SKU. Now it simply assigns `quantity`, causing data loss when the same item is added multiple times.
trigger_condition: When Cart.add() is called with an SKU that already exists in _quantities dictionary

title: Coupon boundary condition changed from < to <= incorrectly rejects valid coupons
explanation: The comparison operator changed from < to <=, altering the business rule for coupon eligibility. Previously, when subtotal equaled coupon.minimum_cents, the coupon would apply (condition was false). Now, when subtotal equals minimum_cents, the condition is true and raises ValueError. For example, with minimum_cents=1000 and subtotal=1000: before allowed the coupon, after rejects it.
trigger_condition: When cart subtotal equals the coupon's minimum_cents threshold exactly

title: Inventory validation no longer uses isolated snapshot
explanation: The comment explicitly states validation should occur on a 'temporary copy', but the code now uses `self._inventory` directly instead of `Inventory(self._inventory.snapshot())`. This means the checkout() calls during validation will modify the real inventory before all lines pass validation, breaking atomicity and potentially leaving inventory in an inconsistent state if later lines fail.
trigger_condition: Diff shows replacement of snapshot() call with direct inventory reference while comment still references temporary copy

title: Partial state modification in reserve_many creates inconsistent inventory
explanation: The refactored reserve_many method now deducts stock inside the loop before validating all items. If validation fails on a later SKU, earlier SKUs have already had their stock reduced without completing the reservation, leaving inventory in an inconsistent state.
trigger_condition: Stock deduction moved inside validation loop instead of being performed after all validations pass
